title: Seller pilot: latency-first sprint deck (prototype)
content:
Slide 1 — title: Latency-first pilot sprint for frictionless onramp
Speaker note: quick intro for SEs and sellers. Keep it under 90s.

Slide 2 — TL;DR for seller (30s):
- What we sell: a low-latency inference pilot that proves consistent p95 < target and cost-per-1000 tokens within agreed band.
- Who it's for: product teams with real-time UX requirements (chat, assistants, search re-rank).
- Ask: 6-week pilot, dataset + 1 integration engineer, 3 success metrics.

Slide 3 — Why latency-first approach (talking bullets):
- Many deals stall because UX jitter kills adoption (not model quality alone).
- We prioritize p95/p99, fallbacks, and autoscaling policy to protect UX.
- Seller soundbite: “We’ll show measurable latency improvement without sacrificing output fidelity.”

Slide 4 — Pilot scope & commitments (operational):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2-week integration + 4-week evaluation).
- Capacity: reserved burst pool (dedicated or hosted reserved cadence).
- Metrics we will instrument: p50/p95/p99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, token cost, error/fallback rate, user conversion delta.
- Deliverables: daily smoke checklist, weekly performance report, final recommendation (scale|quantize|cache).

Slide 5 — Seller checklist before pilot kickoff:
- Confirm target p95 SLA (ms) and acceptable cost range.
- Get sample traffic profile (seq len dist, concurrency).
- Secure dataset access (anonymized) and one integration point (API or SDK).
- Agreement on evaluation prompts/queries + golden set.

Slide 6 — Integration play (tech ops steps, short):
- Sandbox creds provided: link + notes (ops ticket link).
- Default config: batching=auto, cache=on, kv-cache retention=60s, fallback chain: high-quality-large -> quantized-medium -> stub-response with notice.
- Instrumentation: add Redwood tracing header and route name. Add test token for synthetic load.
- Quick test: 20 concurrent sessions, 2 min burst, validate p95.

Slide 7 — Fallback & graceful degradation plan (seller scripts):
- When to trigger: sustained p95 > SLA for 3 consecutive mins or error rate > 1%.
- Fallback chain (example): model-A (full) -> model-A-quant8 -> model-B-lowcost -> cached-prefix -> static short answer with CTA.
- Customer objection line: "We keep UX up while we optimize cost — fallback is instrumented and tracked"

Slide 8 — Measurement & acceptance criteria (what success looks like):
- Primary: p95 <= target for 80% of evaluation windows.
- Secondary: Cost per 1k tokens within agreed band and fallback rate < 5%.
- Business: user completion rate improved by at least X% (define with account).

Slide 9 — Quick demo script for SEs (30–60s demo):
- Show baseline latency under load -> switch to Redwood route with batching/cache -> show tail drop and cost estimate.
- Key visual: side-by-side chart p95, token cost, and fallback events live.

Slide 10 — Common objections + suggested responses (rapid):
- "We can self-host and tune." -> "We provide the runtime + observability and save months of infra work; pilot proves real metrics in production-like conditions."
- "Fallbacks sound risky." -> "We measure fidelity and tag fallback instances so you can see exact UX impact; we only fallback when SLOs at risk."
- "Cost looks high for peak." -> "We model amortized cost including caching and autoscale; pilot includes cost simulation scenarios."

Slide 11 — Risk map & escalation (ops):
- Risk: data access delays -> Mitigation: synthetic dataset plan (owner: seller).
- Risk: model regression on domain prompts -> Mitigation: golden prompt set + eval hooks.
- Escalation path: SE -> Solutions Eng -> Platform SRE -> Customer Success.

Slide 12 — Week-by-week runbook (short):
- Week 0: contract + dataset + success criteria sign-off.
- Week 1–2: integration, smoke tests, baseline metrics.
- Week 3–4: tuned rollout, fallback tuning, cost experiments (quantization, batching).
- Week 5–6: stability window, final report, migrate to reserved if agreed.

Slide 13 — Seller collateral snippets (copy you can paste into email):
- Subject: Pilot to hit your p95 SLA in 6 weeks
- Body intro (short): "We can run a 6-week latency-first pilot that proves your real-world p95 and cost. If we don’t show improvement, we’ll provide an actionable rollback plan."
- CTA: "Can we sync for 30 minutes this week to map your current p95 and traffic profile?"

Slide 14 — TODOs & open questions (working notes):
- Confirm legal signoff on storing anonymized prompts (owner: legal).
- Decide if pilot uses Dedicated or Hosted reserved burst (ops preference: dedicated for predictable p95).
- Add demo dashboard link (PR open: github:repo/infra/pr/412).
- Who will own golden prompt set from customer? (ask during kickoff).

Slide 15 — Appendices / quick references:
- Link: pilot runbook template (confluence:pilot-playbook-123)
- Template JIRA: GTMPILOT-89
- Slack: #pilot-kickoffs (pinned messages: kickoff checklist)

Notes to self (choppy):
- Keep slides short, no deep infra diagrams — SEs want numbers not deep architecture.
- Need 2 one-pagers: (1) exec-level incentivize (faster UX metrics) (2) tech-level (config knobs + tradeoffs).
- Follow up: draft email templates for common verticals (fintech, healthcare, marketplace) with tailored risk lines.

END OF DECK prototype — this is intentionally lightweight, sellers and SEs should iterate per-account.
